title: Next.js development error overlay in a response
description: A Next.js development error overlay element appears in the response body. The overlay prints the failed component, the compile error and often the server-side stack, and it is only rendered by a development build that was shipped to production.
remediation: Build and deploy with NODE_ENV=production so the error overlay is not compiled in, and return a generic error page instead.
limitation: One response body, first 32,768 bytes. It matches the nextjs-portal element the dev overlay mounts; it cannot tell whether the value behind the marker is live or whether the page needs authentication.
scopeT: A response body that carries a Next.js development error overlay element.
fp: A production page that links to a Next.js error page without the portal element is not reported.
recordDesc: A Next.js development error overlay element in a response hands every reader the view the build or admin side kept: The overlay prints the failed component, the compile error and often the server-side stack, and it is only rendered by a development build that was shipped to production.
applicability: Deployments that render a Next.js development error overlay element into a customer- or partner-facing response.
risk: The overlay prints the failed component, the compile error and often the server-side stack, and it is only rendered by a development build that was shipped to production.
why: The marker exists for the build or administrator and answers a question an attacker would otherwise have to guess.
fix: Build and deploy with NODE_ENV=production so the error overlay is not compiled in, and return a generic error page instead.
Keep the build output free of the development overlay by deploying the production bundle only.
verifyT: Request the page again and confirm the response no longer carries a Next.js development error overlay element.
